hunt.justification: Phishing and agent-driven exfiltration bypass traditional perimeter defenses by abusing trusted identities; identifying these chains across surfaces is a priority for data protection.

related.reason: MFA fatigue targets different user behaviors and uses lateral movement rather than direct exfiltration from the entry point.

stages.name: Phishing for Identity and Agent Access
observables: Delivery and execution of malicious attachments

stages.name: Data Exfiltration over C2 Channel
observables: Outbound network connections to external C2 servers

scenario.summary: This attack scenario involves an initial breach via phishing to compromise user identities or local AI agents, followed by the exfiltration of sensitive data over established command-and-control (C2) channels. The campaign specifically targets the unique permissions and access methods of non-human actors and agentic systems, bypassing traditional alert-centric defenses.

meta.rationale: Start with successful logins that bypassed MFA. Focusing on users with high-volume egress reduces the initial scope to active sessions that may be exfiltrating data.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has used a phishing attack to bypass multi-factor authentication and is now using compromised productivity applications to exfiltrate data over a C2 channel.

hunt.name: Detection of Phishing and Agent-Driven Exfiltration
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the transition from initial access via phishing to data theft by correlating identity, process, and network telemetry. It first scopes the estate to successful logins where MFA was not utilized, then scans for rare child processes spawned from common productivity applications and high-volume outbound network traffic to external destinations. An agent weighs these independent signals to find a coordinated attack chain.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, auth_protocol, device_hostname, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND (mfa IS NULL OR LOWER(mfa) = 'false') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find successful authentications where multi-factor authentication was not recorded. These users serve as the primary focus for subsequent behavioral checks.
config.expected_signal: Login rows specifying a user and source IP. Silence suggests all successful logins within the period utilized MFA.

nodes.label: Rare child processes from productivity apps

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, process_name, parent_process_name, process_cmd_line, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{productivity_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(parent_process_name) || ',') > 0 AND NOT (instr(',' || '{{productivity_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{target_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{target_users}}' || ',', ',' || user_name || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_name HAVING host_count <= 3
config.description: Identify unusual applications launched from productivity tools for the targeted users. This isolates execution typically associated with phishing payloads.
config.expected_signal: Rare child processes like cmd.exe or powershell.exe running under an office application for a user with suspicious sign-in activity.

primitive_config.label: Rare child processes from productivity apps
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, process_name, parent_process_name, process_cmd_line, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{productivity_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(parent_process_name) || ',') > 0 AND NOT (instr(',' || '{{productivity_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{target_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{target_users}}' || ',', ',' || user_name || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_name HAVING host_count <= 3
primitive_config.expected: Rare child processes like cmd.exe or powershell.exe running under an office application for a user with suspicious sign-in activity.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, dst_endpoint_ip, SUM(traffic_bytes) AS total_out_bytes, MIN(time) AS first_seen, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE direction = 'outbound' AND ('{{target_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{target_users}}' || ',', ',' || user_name || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND NOT (dst_endpoint_ip LIKE '10.%' OR dst_endpoint_ip LIKE '192.168.%' OR dst_endpoint_ip LIKE '172.%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING total_out_bytes > 5242880 ORDER BY total_out_bytes DESC
config.description: Detect potential exfiltration by identifying large volumes of data sent to external IP addresses associated with the targeted users.
config.expected_signal: Hosts with significant outbound traffic to external IPs that correlates with users identified in the scoping step.

primitive_config.expected: Hosts with significant outbound traffic to external IPs that correlates with users identified in the scoping step.

config.objective: Determine if any host shows a coordinated sequence of suspicious sign-ins, rare process execution from productivity apps, and high-volume exfiltration for the same user.
config.description: The agent correlates the anomalies across identity, process, and network telemetry to identify a confirmed intrusion.
config.expected_signal: Per-host verdicts indicating whether the observed telemetry constitutes a coordinated attack.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign for each host, citing specific rows from all three surfaces.

config.question: the triage-attack-chain verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the triage-attack-chain verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.description: Route the hunt based on the agent's findings.
Contain the host to prevent further data loss.
config.instructions: Isolate the host from the network immediately and collect the suspicious binary for analysis.

config.description: Confirm the agent's verdict and investigate the nature of the exfiltrated data.
config.instructions: Review the cited rows from the triage step. Verify the source of the phishing email if possible and analyze the destination IP reputation. Determine the sensitivity of the data accessed by the process.

config.description: Document findings and update defensive controls.
config.instructions: Record the indicators of compromise (IOCs) and report any MFA bypass techniques discovered. If the child process behavior is confirmed malicious, propose a standing detection rule for the SOC.
